qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: IQVIA possesses significant switching costs and toll-booth properties in its Technology & Analytics Solutions (TAS) segment through its proprietary IMS Health global prescription and sales audit database, which is deeply embedded in biopharma commercial operations. However, over half of revenue is generated by Research & Development Solutions (R&DS, CRO clinical trial execution), which operates in a highly competitive market subject to pharmaceutical RFP bidding pressure, trial cancellations, and biotech funding cyclicality. Competitors like ICON and Medpace prevent excess pricing power. Empirically, IQVIA's 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 8.4% fails the 12% hurdle by a wide margin due to the massive capital base created by the 2016 merger ($16.6B goodwill). Primary erosion threats include sponsor procurement pricing squeeze, commoditization of outsourced clinical labor, and AI automation of clinical trial data management.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 8.4%, REJECT). While IQVIA's IMS prescription data represents an entrenched commercial analytics toll booth, the majority of revenue stems from clinical research organization (CRO) services and IT consulting, which face intense competitive RFP bidding, sponsor price concessions, and cyclical biopharma R&D budget pressures. 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 8.4% (and FY24-FY25 ROIC of ~6.5-8.5%) falls well short of the 12% capital efficiency hurdle, weighed down by a $20B+ invested capital base following the 2016 Quintiles-IMS merger. Furthermore, heavy leverage ($15.7B total debt vs $1.36B net income) and AI exposure across billable clinical trial monitoring labor create significant structural headwinds.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 8.4% (FY2024: ~6.8%, FY2025: ~6.3%) fails the >=12% proof of moat hurdle. FY2025 revenue reached $16,310M with $2,182M operating income (13.4% margin) and $1,361M net income on an invested capital base of ~$21.5B (backed by $16.6B of merger goodwill). Segment breakdown: Research & Development Solutions (R&DS) ~$9.0B (~55% of revenue), Technology & Analytics Solutions (TAS) ~$6.5B (~40%), and Contract Sales & Medical Solutions (CSMS) ~$0.8B (~5%). While TAS benefits from proprietary IMS Health prescription datasets, the dominant R&DS segment relies on billable professional hours (clinical research associates, project managers) subject to competitive RFP bidding against ICON and Medpace, lacking unconstrained pricing power >= inflation. Downstream checks would also fail: Gate 4 faces AI automation headwinds on billable analytics/monitoring labor (CAP <= 10), and Gate 6 fails on balance sheet leverage (Total Debt of $15.72B is ~11.5x GAAP Net Income; Net Debt of ~$13.5B is ~9.9x Net Income vs <=4.0x ceiling; Interest Coverage is ~3.7x-3.9x vs >5.0x hurdle).
